title: Witnessed symmetric choice is strictly stronger than choiceless polynomial time with counting
main_claim: There is one fixed CPT+WSC sentence, over 8 binary relations and with one WSC occurrence, that returns a Boolean value on every finite structure. It is true on the zero-charge Heisenberg-twisted grid structures A_{b^0} and false on the unit-charge structures A_{b^1}. No CPT sentence (with counting and unbounded rank) defines the same class, because every CPT sentence eventually gives the same answer on the pair (A_{b^0}, A_{b^1}).

issues.description: The WSC semantics follow the paper's own summary of Lichter–Schweitzer v3: which arguments the witness term takes, witnesses taken in Aut(A, params, b_0..b_i), and output true if it holds at every terminal fixed point. I could not check this summary against LS2023 offline. Legality of the sentence assumes the summary is faithful. The construction would probably adapt to small differences in convention.
issues.evidence: Lemma sen:history proves that M(α,x) ⊆ Aut(A, α, b_0..b_i), because every element fixes the blocks and fixes x pointwise, and that D(α,x) is an orbit. This is correct for the model as stated in Sec. 1.2.

issues.description: The polynomial bound on the full evaluation trace, including rejected and first-excessive iteration candidates and nested iterations, is given as a syntax-induction sketch rather than with explicit exponents. It is standard and I believe it is correct.
issues.evidence: Every primitive grows hereditary size polynomially. Comprehension ranges are polynomial. Iteration steps act on states that passed the guard, and there are at most P(n)+1 of them.

coverage:
I read every section, 00–08, in full and checked the key steps by hand.
- Heisenberg group law, associativity and commutator: (0, 2B(a,a')) = Σ ω(a_f,a'_f) c^f.
- The action is by automorphisms: divergence is preserved via ∂c^f = 0, and Z_δ is preserved via left-multiplication invariance of g^{-1}g'.
- Sparse-cochain lemma: curl sign conventions on the 12 and 23 faces checked, and the support count L²t0 + L(t12+t13) ≤ Lt holds.
- Small-orbit support: U is isotropic for β_ℓ of rank 2t, so t ≤ a and |T| ≤ 2Lad. The inclusion K_α ⊆ K_0 follows from duality.
- Loomis–Whitney boundary estimate and the giant-component lemma with 6M deleted edges, M = L^{7/4}.
- C^M equivalence via defect-moving bijections: configurations are never placed at w, and p_J avoids T.
- Partial-flow extension and the K-homogeneity formula: variable count r + 7|U| + 6r + 1, and the R_U contradiction argument.
- Forms/molecules transfer: extension counts, equality/membership transfer within 4s ≤ M, orbit-label bijection, and the fibre-size argument within (m+1)s ≤ M.
- Bounded-width CPT description: exact graphs at actual activations, the empty default, the iteration I_j recursion with variable recycling, and Ok via strict-path counting.
- Parameter order: q and m are fixed before L grows, and s = O(L log²L) satisfies the width constraints.
- Upper bound: corner tuple is resolving; match/baseEq recover face vectors; local translation on ≤ 4 faces moves ≤ B atoms and fixes the history; tree-cycle ±1 circulation using the origin's distance labels; the tree elimination test is exact; zero charge gives a unique tree solution and unit charge gives total divergence 1 ≠ 0.

Not done: no symbolic computation was needed beyond hand checks, and I did not verify LS2023's original definitions.
sibling_notes: The board for family 243 was empty when I read it. This paper restates and proves in full the companion's support (Prop. 8), base-equivalence and homogeneity (Props. 11, 13) and transfer (Thm. 14) results, so it does not depend circularly on the companion "CPT does not capture P". Siblings auditing the companion can reuse these checks: small-orbit → K-support via the commutator form, giant component at L^{7/4}, and homogeneity variable count r + 7(6r/c)^{3/2} + 1. I found no gaps in any of them.
